steps.title: Thaw and resuspend PBMCs
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw a vial of frozen PBMCs from a patient or healthy donor, transfer the cells to 5 mL pre‑warmed ImmunoCult™‑XF T‑cell expansion medium in a 15 mL conical tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Activate bulk T cells
steps.instruction: Pellet cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend at 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in ImmunoCult™‑XF medium containing human IL‑7 (5 ng mL⁻¹) and IL‑15 (5 ng mL⁻¹) plus ImmunoCult™ human CD3/CD28/CD2 activator (25 µL mL⁻¹). Plate in a 12‑well (≤2 mL) or 6‑well (≤4 mL) dish and incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for ~72 h.

steps.title: Expand activated T cells
steps.instruction: Collect cells, pellet at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant and resuspend in fresh ImmunoCult™‑XF medium with IL‑7 (5 ng mL⁻¹) and IL‑15 (5 ng mL⁻¹) at ~0.5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹. Plate in 6‑well plates (≤4 mL) or 100 mm dishes (≤10 mL) and culture 5–7 days, changing medium and splitting to ≤1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ every 2–3 days as needed.

steps.title: Cryopreserve expanded T cells
steps.instruction: Reserve 2–5 × 10⁵ cells for flow cytometry; pellet remaining cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in ice‑cold CryoStor® CS10 (0.5 mL per 5 × 10⁵–1 × 10⁶ cells), aliquot into cryovials, place in Mr. Frosty™ at –80 °C overnight, then transfer to liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Prepare cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Wash reserved cells once with 100 µL MACS buffer, pellet 300 × g 5 min 4 °C, discard supernatant. Reconstitute LIVE/DEAD™ Fixable Near‑IR dye (500 µL DMSO) and add 0.2 µL dye to 50 µL MACS buffer per sample (1:250). Incubate cells with dye in 50 µL MACS buffer at 4 °C 10 min protected from light.

steps.title: Surface‑marker staining
steps.instruction: Prepare staining cocktail in 50 µL MACS buffer per sample: BV785‑CD8 (1:200), APC‑CD62L (1:400), PE/Cy7‑CD45RA (1:400), FITC‑CD95 (1:400), BV421‑PD‑1 (1:50), PE/Dazzle594‑TIGIT (1:100). Add 50 µL cocktail to each tube, incubate 15 min at 4 °C protected from light, wash once with 200 µL MACS buffer, resuspend in 100 µL MACS buffer and keep on ice for acquisition.

steps.title: Acquire flow data
steps.instruction: Collect ≥1 × 10⁴–2 × 10⁴ live events per sample, gating sequentially on FSC‑A/SSC‑A (lymphocytes), FSC‑H/FSC‑W & SSC‑H/SSC‑W (singlets), LIVE/DEAD negative (live), then CD8⁺, and finally the surface markers. Include a positive control (activated healthy‑donor T cells).

steps.title: Anneal crRNA and tracrRNA
steps.instruction: In a PCR tube mix 20 µL crRNA (100 pmol) with 20 µL tracrRNA (100 pmol). Heat 95 °C 5 min, then cool on bench 15–25 °C ≥10 min. Store gRNA duplex at –20 °C (up to 1 year).

steps.title: Assemble RNP complexes
steps.instruction: For each 5 × 10⁵ activated T cells, combine 2 µL gRNA duplex (100 pmol) with 0.75 µL Cas9 protein (~50 pmol) (2:1 molar ratio). Incubate 10–20 min at room temperature. If using two gRNAs, prepare two RNPs separately and mix immediately before electroporation.

steps.title: Reactivate frozen T cells for editing
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen expanded T cells (step 4), culture in ImmunoCult™‑XF medium with IL‑2 (25 ng mL⁻¹) and CD3/CD28/CD2 activator (25 µL mL⁻¹) at 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ for 48 h.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Count cells, transfer 5 × 10⁵–1 × 10⁶ cells to a 1.5 mL tube, spin 300 × g 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, wash once with 1 mL PBS, spin again 300 × g 5 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend in electroporation buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 20 µL freshly prepared P3 electroporation buffer (3.6 µL Supplement 1 + 16.4 µL P3 solution). Add the appropriate RNP mixture, pipette up/down 10×, and transfer to a well of a 16‑well nucleocuvette strip.

steps.title: Electroporate T cells
steps.instruction: Run the Lonza 4D‑Nucleofector using program EH‑100. Immediately after the pulse add 75 µL pre‑warmed ImmunoCult™‑XF medium containing IL‑2 (25 ng mL⁻¹) to the cuvette, mix gently, and transfer the suspension to a tube containing an additional 500 µL pre‑warmed medium.

steps.title: Plate electroporated cells
steps.instruction: Aliquot 1/5–2/5 of the cell suspension (≈1 × 10⁵–2 × 10⁵ cells) into 200 µL ImmunoCult™‑XF medium with IL‑2 (25 ng mL⁻¹) per well of a 96‑U‑bottom plate.

steps.title: Add AAV6 donor vector
steps.instruction: Add recombinant AAV6 particles carrying the HDR template to each well at a multiplicity of infection of 1 × 10⁶–2 × 10⁶ genome copies per cell.

steps.title: Add DNA‑PK inhibitor
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL of 50× M3814 stock (250 µM) to each well to achieve a final concentration of 5 µM.

steps.title: Post‑electroporation culture day 1
steps.instruction: After ~16 h, gently pipette cells up/down 10×, pellet 300 × g 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, add 200 µL pre‑warmed ImmunoCult™‑XF medium with IL‑2 (25 ng mL⁻¹) and return to the 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Scale‑up culture day 2
steps.instruction: Approximately 24 h later transfer the entire well content to a 48‑well plate containing 350–400 µL pre‑warmed ImmunoCult™‑XF medium with IL‑2 (25 ng mL⁻¹).

steps.title: Gradual expansion to larger vessels
steps.instruction: Continue expanding cells by sequentially moving cultures from 48‑well → 24‑well (1.5 mL) → 12‑well (3 mL) → 6‑well (up to 10 mL), maintaining IL‑2 (25 ng mL⁻¹) and monitoring density (≤1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹).

steps.title: Switch to IL‑7/IL‑15 maintenance
steps.instruction: Four days after AAV infection replace medium with ImmunoCult™‑XF containing IL‑7 (5 ng mL⁻¹) and IL‑15 (5 ng mL⁻¹) (1.5 mL for 12‑well or 3 mL for 6‑well) and culture for an additional 2 days.

steps.title: Intracellular perforin staining
steps.instruction: Reactivate edited T cells 2 days with IL‑2 (25 ng mL⁻¹) and CD3/CD28/CD2 (25 µL mL⁻¹). Stimulate 1–2 × 10⁵ cells with PMA (50 ng mL⁻¹) and ionomycin (500 ng mL⁻¹) for 6 h in the presence of 1× Brefeldin A. Wash, fix/permeabilize with Cytofix/Cytoperm 20 min at 4 °C (dark), then stain with anti‑perforin antibody (1 µL in 50 µL 1× Perm/Wash) 30 min at 4 °C (dark). Wash twice with 200 µL Perm/Wash, resuspend in 100 µL MACS buffer and acquire by flow cytometry.

steps.title: Genomic DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Lyse 5 × 10⁵–1 × 10⁶ edited T cells in 500 µL QuickExtract™ DNA Extraction Solution, vortex briefly, transfer 50–100 µL lysate to a PCR tube and incubate: 65 °C 15 min → 68 °C 15 min → 95 °C 15 min → hold 4 °C.

steps.title: PCR amplification of target locus
steps.instruction: Set up 25 µL PCR with PrimeSTAR® GXL: 5 µL 5× buffer, 0.5 µL polymerase, 2 µL 2.5 mM dNTPs, 1 µL template DNA (2.5–250 ng), 1 µL each primer (10 µM), water to 25 µL. Run 30 cycles (98 °C 10 s, 60 °C 15 s, 68 °C 1 min kb⁻¹).

steps.title: Clone PCR product
steps.instruction: Purify PCR amplicon, ligate into pJET1.2/Blunt (CloneJET kit), transform into One Shot™ Stbl3 chemically competent E. coli, plate on LB‑agar + 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin, incubate overnight 37 °C.

steps.title: Colony sequencing
steps.instruction: Pick ~100 colonies into a 96‑well plate containing 200 µL LB‑agar + ampicillin, grow overnight 37 °C, submit plasmid DNA with appropriate primers for Sanger sequencing. Analyze traces with ICE or manual alignment to count HDR, NHEJ, and non‑targeted events.

steps.title: Optional: gRNA plasmid testing in HEK293T
steps.instruction: Seed 5 × 10⁵ HEK293T cells per well of a 6‑well plate. Transfect with 3 µg sgRNA‑expression plasmid + 9 µL FuGENE® HD in Opti‑MEM to a final volume of 150 µL (ratio 3:1). After 72 h isolate genomic DNA (50 µL QuickExtract per 10⁵ cells), PCR‑amplify 500–1 000 bp around target, and Sanger‑sequence to assess editing (ICE indel % ≥60 %).

steps.title: Optional: HDR template assembly
steps.instruction: Mix NEBuilder® HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix with 0.5 pmol each of 5′ and 3′ homology arms, codon‑modified exon 3 (or T2A‑cDNA), and NotI‑linearized pAAV‑GFP backbone. Incubate 50 °C 60 min, transform into Stbl3, select colonies, verify insert by Sanger sequencing, and optionally perform NGS for full plasmid verification.

description: Validation of protocol Validation experiments for both gene editing strategies (Figure 1) are shown in our article Li et al. [2], as follows: PRF1 gene editing conditions were optimized using T cells from healthy donors [Figure 5 and Table S1; one independent experiment per donor (n = 3)]. Efficient repair of perforin mutations in T cells from a patient with FHL2 was demonstrated in Figure 6, Table S1, and Suppl. Figure S4 [four independent experiments (n = 4)]. Patient T cells showed a T SCM -like phenotype after gene repair [Figure 6D; four independent experiments (n = 4)] and did not show increased levels of the T-cell exhaustion markers PD-1, TIGIT, TIM-3, LAG-3, and CD39 [Figure 6E and Suppl. Figure S5; four independent experiments (n = 4)].
